The Rousseau neighbourhood is located in West Beaumont, east of Range Road 243 and north of Montrose and Four Seasons Estates as shown in Attachment 1. The purpose of the proposed bylaw 98220 is to amend the Land Use Bylaw by redistricting the undeveloped areas of the neighbourhood from Agricultural Holdings District to Conventional Neighbourhood and Integrated Neighbourhood Districts as shown in Attachment 2. The redistricting will allow for the development of the Integrated Neighbourhood parcel as a combined school park site. The site will accommodate a Kindergarten to Grade 12 Francophone school for which funding was identified in late 2019 and early 2020 and for which Council approved site preparation funding in April 2020. The redistricting will also allow the remaining land to be developed as a low-density residential neighbourhood as contemplated in the Rousseau outline plan provided in Attachment 3. The school site is located on a parcel in the southeast portion of the planned area identified as Municipal Reserve in this outline plan. The Municipal Government Act allows Municipal Reserve to be used as a public park or recreation area or for school board purposes. The school yard is to be developed in accordance with the direction provided in the outline plan and the site is to be redistricted to Integrated Neighbourhood for consistency with most other school sites in Beaumont. The Conventional Neighbourhood District that is proposed for the rest of the Rousseau neighbourhood is used for all other established neighbourhoods in the city outside of the Inner Ring Road including the parts of Rousseau that have already been developed. It supports lower density forms of residential development as contemplated in the outline plan. Both land use districts also permit parks, open space, trail connections and stormwater management facilities to be developed as envisioned in the outline plan. As a result of the circulation of this proposal and the notice of public hearing, administration has received a number of comments. You've received redacted copies of these comments in attachment four. No concerns were raised specifically about the Integrated Neighbourhood and Conventional Neighbourhood Districts that are proposed. There were some inquiries to confirm the location and construction timing of stormwater management facilities in the Conventional Neighbourhood area and to confirm also that the Leblanc Canal is planned to remain green space following the redistricting. There was also one comment generally in support of the proposal. Additionally there were some comments from residents in opposition to the proposal with concerns focused on the selection process for the school site which is beyond the scope of this redistricting as well as on the potential for traffic, noise, privacy and the aesthetic impacts of a school near their homes. Administration has documented these concerns and will work to address them at the development permit stage through a transportation impact assessment and our review of building and site design and landscaping. Overall administration's view is that this redistricting proposal is consistent with the city's overall policy framework and the resale land use concept as set out in the outline plan and so therefore we are supporting the adoption of this amendment.
